records.quote: Cloud significantly accelerated with revenues growing 48%, now on an annual run rate of over $70 billion. Backlog grew by 55% quarter-over-quarter to $240 billion, representing a wide breadth of customers, driven by demand for AI products.
records.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

records.quote: Overall, we’re seeing our AI investments and infrastructure drive revenue and growth across the board. To meet customer demand and capitalize on the growing opportunities ahead of us, our 2026 CapEx investments are anticipated to be in the range of $175 billion to $185 billion.
records.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google
Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

records.quote: Today, I’ll provide an update on our AI progress and then share highlights from Search, Cloud, YouTube, and Waymo.
records.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

records.quote: Next, Google Cloud.
records.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

records.quote: Nearly 75% of Google Cloud customers have used our vertically optimized AI, from chips, to models, to AI platforms, and enterprise AI agents which offer superior performance, quality, security, and cost-efficiency. These AI customers use 1.8x as many products as those who do not, enabling us to diversify our product portfolio, deepen customer relationships and accelerate revenue growth.
records.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

records.quote: We offer leading infrastructure for AI training and inference to our Cloud customers, with the industry’s widest variety of compute options: from our own seventh-generation Ironwood TPU to the latest NVIDIA GPUs. Our ten-year track record in building our own accelerators—with expertise in chips, systems, networking, and software—translates to leading power and performance efficiency for large-scale inference and training.
records.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

records.quote: Our Cloud AI accelerators serve the leading frontier AI labs, capital markets firms like Citadel Securities, enterprises like Mercedes-Benz, and governments for high-performance computing applications.
records.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

records.quote: We also offer our leading generative AI models, including Gemini, Imagen, Veo, Chirp, and Lyria to Cloud customers. In December alone, nearly 350 customers each processed more than 100 billion tokens. In Q4, revenue from products built on our generative AI models grew nearly 400% year-over-year, significantly accelerating from the prior quarter. Today, more than 120,000 enterprises use Gemini, including AI unicorns like Lovable and OpenEvidence, and global enterprises like Airbus and Honeywell. 95% of the top 20, and over 80% of the top hundred SaaS companies use Gemini, including Salesforce and Shopify. Gemini is becoming the AI engine for the world's most successful software companies.
records.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

records.quote: Before moving on, I’m pleased that we are collaborating with Apple as their preferred Cloud provider and to develop the next generation of Apple Foundation Models, based on Gemini technology.
records.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

records.quote: I would start by joining Sundar in how pleased I am that we are collaborating with Apple as their preferred Cloud provider and to develop the next generation of Apple Foundation Models, based on Gemini technology.
records.speaker: Philipp Schindler, SVP and CBO, Google

records.quote: We partnered with Reliance Jio to provide over 500 million consumers with an 18-month free trial of our Gemini suite of products and two terabytes of cloud storage. Reliance’s enterprise customers will also get access to Google Cloud’s Gemini Enterprise and TPUs, bringing the best of Google AI to every employee and workflow.
records.speaker: Philipp Schindler, SVP and CBO, Google

records.quote: The Home Depot is applying Google AI across the board, from Cloud tools to AI-powered ads and YouTube creator partnerships that connect with the next generation of do’ers. Their investments in PMax and YouTube Creator Partnerships have resulted in double-digit increase in ad clicks and visits.
records.speaker: Philipp Schindler, SVP and CBO, Google

records.quote: Moving to Q4 performance, we delivered strong growth in the fourth quarter. Consolidated revenues reached $113.8 billion, up 18%, or 17% in constant currency, and was driven by an acceleration in Search and Cloud revenues.
records.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

records.quote: The Google Cloud segment delivered outstanding results in the fourth quarter as the business continued to benefit from strong demand for our enterprise AI products.
records.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

records.quote: Cloud revenue accelerated meaningfully and was up 48% to $17.7 billion. Revenues were driven by strong performance in GCP, which continued to grow at a rate that was much higher than Cloud's overall revenue growth rate. As Sundar noted, we're driving performance through strong growth and a win rate of new customers, signing larger customer commitments, and increasing spend with existing customers.
records.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

records.quote: Cloud operating income was $5.3 billion, more than doubling year-over-year. And operating margin increased from 17.5% in the fourth quarter of last year, to 30.1%.
records.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

records.quote: Google Cloud's backlog increased 55% sequentially and more than doubled year-over-year, reaching $240 billion at the end of the fourth quarter. The increase in backlog was driven by strong demand for our Cloud products, led by our enterprise AI offerings from multiple customers.
records.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

records.quote: CapEx was $27.9 billion for the fourth quarter, and $91.4 billion for the full year, in line with our expectation. The vast majority of our CapEx was invested in technical infrastructure, with approximately 60% of that investment in servers and 40% in data centers and networking equipment.
records.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

records.quote: In Google Cloud, we're seeing significant demand for our products and services, which we expect to continue to drive strong growth, despite the tight supply environment we're operating in.
records.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

records.quote: For the full year 2026, we expect CapEx to be in the range of $175 billion to $185 billion, with investments ramping over the course of the year.
records.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google
Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google
records.quote: For the full year 2026, we expect CapEx to be in the range of $175 billion to $185 billion, with investments ramping over the course of the year.
records.definition: Management CapEx terminology; equivalence to GAAP cash-payments metric not assumed

records.quote: We're investing in AI compute capacity to support frontier model development by Google DeepMind, ongoing efforts to improve the user experience, and drive higher advertiser ROI in Google Services, significant Cloud customer demand, as well as strategic investments in Other Bets.
records.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

records.quote: Keep in mind that the availability of supply, pricing of components, and timing of cash payments can cause some variability in the reported CapEx number.
records.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

records.quote: In 2025, depreciation increased by nearly $6 billion, or 38%, from $15.3 billion in 2024, to $21.1 billion in 2025. Given the increase in our CapEx investments in recent years, we expect the growth rate in 2026 depreciation to accelerate in Q1, and meaningfully increase for the full year.
records.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

records.quote: We're also planning to continue hiring in key investment areas, such as AI and Cloud.
records.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

records.quote: All the innovation we are doing, be it Imagen, Veo, Lyria, Genie, all that work we bring into our products and to our Cloud customers; and YouTube is going to be a natural place for creators.
records.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

records.quote: and we've been supply-constrained, even as we've been ramping up our capacity. Obviously, our CapEx spend this year is an eye towards the future; and you have to keep in mind some of the time horizons are increasing in the supply chain, et cetera.
records.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

records.quote: I expect the demand we are seeing across the board, across our services, what we need to invest for future work for Google DeepMind, as well as for Cloud, I think is exceptionally strong. And so I do expect to go through the year in a supply-constrained way.
records.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

records.quote: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google: Doug look, I think the LLM frontier, it's been an exciting trajectory, and I think 2026 will continue to show that progress. We're obviously improving these models across many paradigms, on pre-training, post-training, test time compute, and so on. And we are bringing multimodal models into the picture. We are bringing agentic capabilities, coding areas showing a lot of progress. And obviously, integrating all of this together and offering a great customer experience through our products, as well as through our APIs, to our Cloud customers. To me, feels like there's a lot of headroom ahead.
records.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

records.quote: In terms of TPUs, I would think about it as it's reflected in our overall part of what makes Google Cloud an attractive choice is the wide choice of accelerators we bring to bear here, and we meet customers in terms of what their needs are, and the choice, as well as other things we bring as part of Google Cloud.
records.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

records.quote: The end-to-end efficiencies in our data centers, all of that comes to bear, and that's what you see in the strong momentum in Google Cloud. And given the overall investment we are making, we expect to be able to drive that momentum there. So that's how I would think about it.
records.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

records.quote: The first one is the total investment that we make across the company. This was, for example, in 2025, the $91 billion we invested in CapEx and our estimate for CapEx investment this year, so what's the total envelope that we want to invest to ensure that we can drive both near-term and long-term growth for the company.
records.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

records.quote: I know within Cloud, it's very obvious external, but you've heard the comments on the success we're seeing in Search, the comments from Sundar and from Philipp; and then the frontier model development that really serves as the foundation for the organization.
records.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

records.quote: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google: Thanks, Michael. Obviously, people go through a lot of commercial journeys across many of our surfaces: Search, YouTube, Gemini App and so on. So I think as well as we support, through Cloud and Ads, our entire Retail partners as well.
records.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

records.quote: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google: And the question with regard to the CapEx and what makes up the total that we've announced for this year and last year.
records.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

records.quote: Another important component is how we allocate this CapEx, and we've commented in the past about the allocation of our ML compute across the business. And for 2026, just over half of our ML compute is expected to go towards the Cloud business.
records.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

tev-40397c8874aaf2474f53.quote: Your first question comes from Brian Nowak with Morgan Stanley. Your line is now open.
tev-40397c8874aaf2474f53.speaker: Operator

tev-9c0378fa1ed8cd12731f.quote: Brian Nowak (Morgan Stanley): Thanks for taking my questions. I have two. One on agentic, one on YouTube.
tev-9c0378fa1ed8cd12731f.speaker: Brian Nowak (Morgan Stanley)

tev-108e3858d328c0e52f7f.quote: The first one on agentic, Sundar, I'd be curious to hear about, as you look back at 2025, where do you think you made the most progress on new types of agentic commerce products?
tev-108e3858d328c0e52f7f.speaker: Brian Nowak (Morgan Stanley)

tev-56d03b301da8a8be4709.quote: And then looking into '26, where are you most optimistic for even more progress and utility for users and your advertisers?
tev-56d03b301da8a8be4709.speaker: Brian Nowak (Morgan Stanley)

tev-95ad53422dec74523e6c.quote: And the second one is on YouTube. We've seen a lot of the new content-creation models like Genie, et cetera. Walk us through the Alphabet long-term vision for how Genie and some of these content-creation tools could be integrated into YouTube over time.
tev-95ad53422dec74523e6c.speaker: Brian Nowak (Morgan Stanley)

tev-b65d793109a94b633cfc.quote: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google: Great. Thanks, Brian.
tev-b65d793109a94b633cfc.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

tev-e6b35b1b6afe15f32b6e.quote: First, maybe I'll take the agentic part first.
tev-e6b35b1b6afe15f32b6e.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

tev-efd762f47056c79a27ea.quote: You know, I definitely think '25 was more about laying the foundation, getting the models to start being more robust in agentic use cases. Obviously, coding is the area where the progress was the most felt.
tev-efd762f47056c79a27ea.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

tev-d7add19a010ca3bc0a4b.quote: In the areas like commerce, I think we spent the year working with the ecosystem to develop the underlying protocol that's going to be needed for this agentic world. So I think the launch of Universal Commerce Protocol at NRF in January with a bunch of partners, founding partners, I think has been super well-received.
tev-d7add19a010ca3bc0a4b.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

tev-06488cc34050ed2320bc.quote: So, I'm excited now that we have laid the foundation of interoperability on which agentic commerce can work. And now we are integrating those experiences into Gemini, AI Mode and so on.
tev-06488cc34050ed2320bc.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

tev-48fe902683beb142dda5.quote: So I think this is the year where you will see consumers actually being able to use all of this, and I'm excited about the opportunity ahead.
tev-48fe902683beb142dda5.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

tev-bdfcc0566966945c9e9c.quote: On YouTube, look, super excited by Genie. I'm blown away by -- I've spent a lot of time creating these incredible worlds.
tev-bdfcc0566966945c9e9c.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

tev-45af0ca8350228613325.quote: I think it's going to have a wide level of applicability. I think an area where we shine in general is multimodality and representing the real world, and I think Genie is a further step in that direction in terms of building world models.
tev-45af0ca8350228613325.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

tev-2c5ad9c6bc273b9f5473.quote: We are going to keep incorporating these tools. Already creators are responding by adopting these. But we do want to put creators at the center of the experience, and that's very, very important to us. And so it's, for us, making sure YouTube is a voice for creator expression as the foundation by which we will approach this.
tev-2c5ad9c6bc273b9f5473.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

tev-0b5a8a2f2dc227f66d03.quote: Brian Nowak (Morgan Stanley): Great. Thanks, Sundar.
tev-0b5a8a2f2dc227f66d03.speaker: Brian Nowak (Morgan Stanley)

tev-713d7f2e69b745c3b91a.quote: Operator: Your next question comes from Eric Sheridan with Goldman Sachs. Your line is now open.
tev-713d7f2e69b745c3b91a.speaker: Operator

tev-6b0a897f8303a81de35f.quote: Eric Sheridan (Goldman Sachs): Thanks so much for taking the question. Two, if I could.
tev-6b0a897f8303a81de35f.speaker: Eric Sheridan (Goldman Sachs)

tev-b580632eed5f811aabd9.quote: Over the last couple of earnings calls, we talked a lot about imbalances between demand and capacity for AI, both internally and externally. With the step function change and absolute capital dollars you're projecting now in '26, can you talk about the pathway of closing the gaps for the need for compute, both internally and externally and how to think about some of the outputs of closing that gap as the year progresses?
tev-b580632eed5f811aabd9.speaker: Eric Sheridan (Goldman Sachs)

tev-6b155e66a45a2437a3e4.quote: And again, the second part would be against that level of spend that you're now projecting toward '26, how do you think about continuing to find operating efficiencies inside the business to fund those growth investments as well? Thank you.
tev-6b155e66a45a2437a3e4.speaker: Eric Sheridan (Goldman Sachs)

tev-1b6784d966ec89061756.quote: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google: Thanks, Eric. You know, you are right,
tev-1b6784d966ec89061756.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

tev-851319650d6efe542560.quote: So, we are constantly planning for the long-term and working towards that. And, obviously, how we close the gap this year is a function of what we have done in the prior years. And so there is that time delay to keep in mind.
tev-851319650d6efe542560.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

tev-799134ce698168bbda99.quote: And maybe Anat can touch on the second part.
tev-799134ce698168bbda99.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

tev-51fa67fb36694e27baaf.quote: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google: Thanks, Eric, for the question.
tev-51fa67fb36694e27baaf.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

tev-a34772e54f6dc33ca104.quote: I've mentioned on one of the previous earnings calls our approach to how we look at efficiency and productivity, and we don't view this as an episodic one-time project or effort, but rather how we run the business on a regular basis, and always seek additional opportunities to drive efficiency across the business.
tev-a34772e54f6dc33ca104.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

tev-b64e0a8bc498b9c14d0e.quote: And certainly, with the demand we're seeing, whether it's from external customers or across the organization, the more capital we can free up within the organization to invest, the better we can turn this flywheel of making investments to drive future growth.
tev-b64e0a8bc498b9c14d0e.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

tev-82d9076c8183ac5a3ab9.quote: And we're doing this across the organization, whether it's within our technical infrastructure, certainly when we invest at these amounts, we look at how we can ensure that we are the most efficient with every dollar that goes towards our technical infrastructure.
tev-82d9076c8183ac5a3ab9.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

tev-6fd72935c6376b1aa5cb.quote: There are scientific innovations that are part of that process, technical innovation, as you know, and we've mentioned before, we primarily focus on construction of our own data centers. We do partner with some external parties on lease on occasion, but most of our data centers we can start ourselves, and we ensure that we do it in the most efficient way, in a way that matches our workloads and our needs.
tev-6fd72935c6376b1aa5cb.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

tev-5da72a3f4fda8e7014dc.quote: We look at coding productivity that Sundar mentioned in the past. About 50% of our codes are written by agents, coding agents, which are then reviewed by our own engineers. But certainly, it helps our engineers do more, move faster with the current footprint.
tev-5da72a3f4fda8e7014dc.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

tev-1b7c98becd6be0b96191.quote: We look at how we run the business across the organization. So using AI within the
tev-1b7c98becd6be0b96191.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

tev-718b990c2bb134065e9d.quote: business to drive daily operations. It can be all the way from the engineering team to small teams within our back office. Even within my Finance team, for example, we deployed the agents within our treasury organization. We're deploying agents within how we run, how we pay and reconcile invoices, et cetera.
tev-718b990c2bb134065e9d.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

tev-ca68cd56fe860c948bdf.quote: So there are opportunities across the business that we evaluate on a regular basis to ensure we can free up more of that capacity to invest in our future.
tev-ca68cd56fe860c948bdf.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

tev-7aff5d62effb4cfdd7e2.quote: Operator: Your next question comes from Doug Anmuth with JP Morgan. Your line is now open.
tev-7aff5d62effb4cfdd7e2.speaker: Operator

tev-8f3d08c0ea2b6406c254.quote: Douglas Anmuth (JP Morgan): Thanks for taking questions. I have two. Over the last couple years, we've seen considerable large language model leapfrogging, and many expect that to continue. What are the ways that Google can build and maintain its Gemini position around data and distribution and product integration?
tev-8f3d08c0ea2b6406c254.speaker: Douglas Anmuth (JP Morgan)

tev-8e776d07ff1c4ae14925.quote: And then, how should we think about the potential for TPUs to move outside of Google Cloud and into external data centers and develop as an incremental revenue stream? Thank you.
tev-8e776d07ff1c4ae14925.speaker: Douglas Anmuth (JP Morgan)

tev-0df8157f9e45e56f2e8b.quote: And as you have seen our trajectory over the past two years, in terms of how we've been making progress, I think we are in a very, very relentless innovation cadence, and I think we are confident about maintaining that momentum as we go through '26.
tev-0df8157f9e45e56f2e8b.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

tev-a1b3cfe02a8b85f2aa01.quote: Douglas Anmuth (JP Morgan): Thank you, Sundar.
tev-a1b3cfe02a8b85f2aa01.speaker: Douglas Anmuth (JP Morgan)

tev-0200785fcda73a7bb968.quote: Operator: Your next question comes from Mark Shmulik with AllianceBernstein. Your line is now open.
tev-0200785fcda73a7bb968.speaker: Operator

tev-b7b437f5e748f5534608.quote: Mark Shmulik (Bernstein): Yes, thanks for taking my questions. Two, if I may.
tev-b7b437f5e748f5534608.speaker: Mark Shmulik (Bernstein)

tev-3815b6f35b5c221ec216.quote: The first for Anat. Can you talk a little bit more about the relationship between investment levels and how you expect core performance to trend? Is there an operating income or free cash flow objective that you solve towards? How do you think about greenlighting resources and projects?
tev-3815b6f35b5c221ec216.speaker: Mark Shmulik (Bernstein)

tev-5fcc1bfd6492080dbf80.quote: And the second question is for all of you. A year ago, you probably could have guessed the answer to this question. But given where we are today, for each of you, what keeps you up at night here as you think about the Google story and what's next? Thanks.
tev-5fcc1bfd6492080dbf80.speaker: Mark Shmulik (Bernstein)

tev-16e1e9a1b1f69e315bdd.quote: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google: Thanks, Mark. Let me start with the question on the investment framework, and it's an important one and as you can imagine, an important one for us as well.
tev-16e1e9a1b1f69e315bdd.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

tev-1f5ff9f43e0b53e6c095.quote: We have a highly rigorous framework that we use internally where we look at all the needs for investment, whether it's from our own organization, or from external customers, and have an estimate of what that investment could potentially yield. Obviously, not just near-term but long-term as well. So we take that into consideration when we make the following decision.
tev-1f5ff9f43e0b53e6c095.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

tev-6a727c89bedeb7a1b7a2.quote: And then the second way we use that framework is to allocate these funds across the organization, determine where we should make these investments.
tev-6a727c89bedeb7a1b7a2.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

tev-49e69d445c4e5e309769.quote: And throughout the year, as you can imagine, we always look to understand where things are moving, whether it's the external dynamics or internal dynamics. And I've mentioned some of the supply chain pressures we're seeing externally. So we look at this with a highly rigorous framework to make sure that we're making the right decision.
tev-49e69d445c4e5e309769.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

tev-06e1fd7f14ed5cfaa244.quote: It was exciting to see the fact that we're already monetizing -- and you saw it in the results that we just issued this quarter -- the investments that we've made in AI. It's already delivering results across the business.
tev-06e1fd7f14ed5cfaa244.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

tev-74c7437541ea13bf4b9a.quote: We then also look at just the cash flow, cash flow generation, the health of our financials
tev-74c7437541ea13bf4b9a.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

tev-afef8231e026695ab65c.quote: and the balance sheet. That's important as well. So we take that into consideration when we make the decision about the overall level of investment. We want to make sure that we do it in a fiscally responsible way, and that we invest appropriately but we do it in a way that maintains a very healthy financial position for the organization.
tev-afef8231e026695ab65c.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

tev-3548d5c847419ca01d58.quote: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google: Maybe I can answer on what keeps us up at night.
tev-3548d5c847419ca01d58.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

tev-0e2e27c4d6dbb2461e68.quote: Look, I think overall, we've been on this AI-first trajectory for over a decade now, and it's what we've been methodically thinking our way through. It's the reason why we have been working on TPUs for over a decade, as an example.
tev-0e2e27c4d6dbb2461e68.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

tev-5d83f649d5aedaa06738.quote: But I think specifically at this moment, maybe the top question is definitely around compute capacity, all the constraints, be it power, land, supply chain constraints, how you ramp up to meet this extraordinary demand for this moment. Get our investments right for the long-term and do it all in a way that we are driving efficiencies and doing it in a world-class way.
tev-5d83f649d5aedaa06738.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

tev-2978290ebaa88ce835ea.quote: So that's where I think we are meeting the moment well, but it's definitely an area where we're spending a lot of time.
tev-2978290ebaa88ce835ea.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

tev-3b2bf5bc8d447488220b.quote: Operator: The next question comes from Michael Nathanson with MoffettNathanson. Your line is now open.
tev-3b2bf5bc8d447488220b.speaker: Operator

tev-fc35c87f6ddc8489bf8c.quote: Michael Nathanson (MoffettNathanson): Thanks. I have one for Sundar and one for Anat.
tev-fc35c87f6ddc8489bf8c.speaker: Michael Nathanson (MoffettNathanson)

tev-2950939b34ccb010e338.quote: Sundar, you mentioned Universal Commerce Protocol a bunch of times. I wonder if you could spend some time talking about the rationale for developing it, the opportunity that you see it solves for, and what it means for the product discovery funnel for consumers.
tev-2950939b34ccb010e338.speaker: Michael Nathanson (MoffettNathanson)

tev-313a5efb3fe1e81ac874.quote: And then for Anat, any color you can provide on a CapEx guide between longer-duration assets, like buildings and infrastructure, and shorter cycle assets, like technical and audio equipment, that would be helpful. Thanks.
tev-313a5efb3fe1e81ac874.speaker: Michael Nathanson (MoffettNathanson)

tev-17c9b8aab6873d8a0e1f.quote: The opportunity to improve the experience, I think, can be kind of a huge foundational uplift here. But it's important that we are approaching it, keeping in mind that our users, as well as merchants here and figuring out that value.
tev-17c9b8aab6873d8a0e1f.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

tev-314ff20cba2d618a71cb.quote: Part of what's been good in designing the Universal Commerce Protocol is it makes it much easier for users to complete transactions. But at the same time, it allows merchants to help showcase the range of their offerings, if they want to make promotions, et cetera. So all of that is built into the protocol.
tev-314ff20cba2d618a71cb.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

tev-a1902dcdf9e83fb169be.quote: And I think you have to get that value prop for the ecosystem right to make the experience better.
tev-a1902dcdf9e83fb169be.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

tev-fcf8d1b5d5277ccb25ac.quote: And so it's foundational. And more importantly, we are now implementing the protocols, and our Gemini models are making progress in those agentic capabilities.
tev-fcf8d1b5d5277ccb25ac.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

tev-9e81fee9a800a5316e55.quote: So, I'm excited about a future where, as people are going through discovery, searching, finding new things, if they're interested in acting upon it, all of that is seamless; and so it overall creates an expansionary moment.
tev-9e81fee9a800a5316e55.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

tev-b107935e3fface16440d.quote: Approximately 60% of our investment in 2025, and it's going to be fairly similar in 2026, went towards machines; so, the servers. And then 40% is what you would refer to as long duration assets, which is our data centers and networking equipment.
tev-b107935e3fface16440d.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

tev-835539d909c77d2ae06c.quote: I think you're probably referring to the depreciation delta between them, those long-term duration assets depreciate over -- the building could be 40 years or longer. Other components may be less than that.
tev-835539d909c77d2ae06c.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

tev-c4658e248f6fc9b0c975.quote: Michael Nathanson (MoffettNathanson): Thank you so much.
tev-c4658e248f6fc9b0c975.speaker: Michael Nathanson (MoffettNathanson)
